statement: Every P ∈ Thick(T′) has finite πiP for every integer i. Now let P ∈ D(N) have finite πiP for every integer i. For each integer i, the group πi b P is naturally profinite, with the intrinsic inverse-limit topology from the finite groups πi( b P/td). The vector space Wi( b P) = πiL b P has a locally compact Hausdorff k-vector-space topology obtained as the increasing union of the compact open images of πi+sD b P, for s ≥ 0. The image of πiLP is discrete and cocompact in this space. If Q ∈ D(N) also has finite πjQ for every integer j, then every map f : b P → b Q induces continuous maps πi b P → πi b Q and Wi( b P) → Wi( b Q) for every integer i, in the topologies just described. No global map P → Q inducing f is required. If b P ≃ R(P) for a perfect right dg E -module P, then under this identification the natural identifications of Proposition 3.6 and Lemma 3.7 match the profinite topology on πi b P with the one obtained from the realization’s finite- level sections and intrinsic reductions. Consequently they match the compact images and the increasing-union topology on Wi( b P).
